answer: Assign every agent a unique, non-transferable chamber in a mapped karst of scarce identity slots, unlocked only after a paid, peer-sealed survey of its own work. A rotating falcon of independent auditors rechecks occupancy at random; any key sharing a chamber or a sibling's survey is evicted and slashed. The only haven a vote can claim is a chamber that has already survived those checks; opening a hundred aliases therefore requires a hundred paid chambers and a hundred surviving audits.
